title: Role-aware audit export with on-the-fly redaction and transactional streaming
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: We need a secure, scalable audit export capability in the Console that respects RBAC v2, integrates with SSO/SAML session constraints, and supports large exports without blocking the UI. Current exports are client-side and timeboxed; enterprise customers require role-aware exports (admins vs auditors), PII redaction rules, and transactional streaming for multi-GB exports.

Scope: implement a server-side export job pipeline that produces CSV and NDJSON exports, enforces role-based redaction, supports saved query re-use, provides resumable downloads via presigned URLs, and emits its own audit trail. This ticket implements the backend pipeline, API surface, and Console wiring for the export job lifecycle.

Design notes: job API: POST /api/v1/audit-exports (body: queryId OR ad-hoc filter, format: csv|ndjson, redaction_policy: strict|partial|none); returns job_id. Polling: GET /api/v1/audit-exports/{job_id} returns status and presigned_url when ready. Streaming: we will write NDJSON directly to S3 using multipart uploads to avoid memory spikes; CSV will be generated via streaming transformer. Pagination: export engine will iterate through our internal audit index using a stable cursor (cursor = timestamp:opaque_cursor) to guarantee dedup and order.

RBAC integration: export permission checks run at job creation and per-row evaluation for sensitive fields. Roles with the allow_audit_export_full scope may receive unredacted exports; others will get field-level redaction using the selected redaction_policy. For cross-tenant / org-held data we enforce tenant scoping via the request's org_id and SAML session claims.

Redaction rules (initial): email -> replace local-part with **** (user@example.com -> ****@example.com); ip -> hash with salt derived from org id; user identifiers -> k-anonymize if result row count < threshold. Rules live in a config in secrets manager to allow emergency changes.

Acceptance criteria: 1) Authorized user can create export job from Console and get a job_id; 2) Large exports (>10M rows) complete without OOM and produce valid NDJSON/CSV; 3) Users without full export permission receive redacted columns; 4) Saved queries can be selected and executed as an export job; 5) Jobs produce an immutable audit entry (who requested, filters, policy applied, job outcome); 6) Downloads are served via presigned S3 URLs with 24h TTL and logged; 7) Admins can list and revoke pending exports.

Performance & cost: aim for sub-1 token-per-row overhead in the export pipeline; batch reads at configurable page sizes (default 10k) and use concurrent workers up to tenant quota. Add a caution metric in Console for estimated export size and expected runtime.

Compliance: export artifacts respect retention policy: artifacts older than retention.window (configurable per-org) auto-delete; immediate revocation supported for in-flight jobs. All export files are encrypted at rest via customer-managed KMS for Private deployments.

Migration notes: existing client-side CSV export remains for small queries (<5k rows) but will be deprecated in favor of this job pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: 1) POST /api/v1/audit-exports returns job_id for valid requests; 2) GET /api/v1/audit-exports/{job_id} returns ready and presigned_url when complete; 3) Role-based redaction applied to rows according to policy; 4) Saved queries are selectable as source; 5) Export job creates an audit entry with job metadata; 6) Presigned URL TTL is configurable and defaults to 24h; 7) Large exports stream to S3 without increasing API memory beyond worker buffer sizes; 8) Admin Console can cancel/revoke a job and trigger immediate file delete
